arxiv-1807-01240.title: On the Incomparability of Cache Algorithms in Terms of Timing Leakage
arxiv-1807-01240.creator: Pablo Cañones, Boris Köpf, Jan Reineke
arxiv-1807-01240.description: Abstract . Modern computer architectures rely on caches to reduce the latency gap between the CPU and main memory. While indispensable for performance, caches pose a serious threat to security because they leak information about memory access patterns of programs via execution time.

arxiv-2001-11725.title: Yu-Shiba-Rusinov states of single magnetic molecule in an s − w ​ a ​ v ​ e s-wave superconductor
arxiv-2001-11725.creator: Saurabh Pradhan, Jonas Fransson
arxiv-2001-11725.description: Abstract We use the numerical renormalization group theory to investigate the Yu-Shiba-Rusinov (YSR) bound state properties of single magnetic molecules placed in an s-wave superconducting substrate. The molecule consist of a large core spin and a single orbital, coupled via an exchange interaction.

arxiv-2311-04600.title: A Deep Learning Based Resource Allocator for Communication Systems with Dynamic User Utility Demands
arxiv-2311-04600.creator: Pourya Behmandpoor, Mark Eisen, Panagiotis Patrinos, Marc Moonen
arxiv-2311-04600.description: Abstract Deep learning (DL) based resource allocation (RA) has recently gained significant attention due to its performance efficiency. However, most related studies assume an ideal case where the number of users and their utility demands, e.g., data rate constraints, are fixed, and the designed DL-based RA scheme exploits a policy trained only for these fixed parameters.

arxiv-2311-06992.title: Ball-AR: Fostering Playful Co-Located Interaction Through Environment-centric Physical Activity with AR DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX CCS: Human-centered computing Collaborative and social computing devices
arxiv-2311-06992.creator: Arnav Kumar, Andrés Monroy-Hernández
arxiv-2311-06992.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Arnav Kumar, Andrés Monroy-Hernández. We present Ball-AR, an augmented reality (AR) game where two players in the same physical space attempt to hit each other with virtual dodgeballs overlaid on the physical world. Researchers have studied AR’s potential for fostering co-located interaction and physical activity; however, they have not investigated the impacts of physical activity and physical environment on user experiences and interaction. We created an AR dodgeball game centered around encouraging physical activity and harnessing the physical environment.

arxiv-2504-16575.title: Impact of a tunneling particle on the quantum state of a barrier: two-particle wave-packet model
arxiv-2504-16575.creator: Roman Michelko, Peter Bokes
arxiv-2504-16575.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Roman Michelko, Peter Bokes. We investigate the scattering of two distinguishable particles with unequal masses and a mutual short-range interaction with the aim of quantifying the impact of a tunneling “projectile” particle on the quantum mechanical state of the “barrier” particle.

pmc-10710968.title: Parasites of firebugs in Austria with focus on the “micro”-diversity of the cosmopolitan trypanosomatid Leptomonas pyrrhocoris
pmc-10710968.creator: Alexei Yu. Kostygov, Ľubomíra Chmelová, Julia Reichl, Alexandra Jászayová, Jan Votýpka, Hans-Peter Fuehrer, Vyacheslav Yurchenko

pmc-10757473.title: Upadacitinib in end stage renal disease: A case of acute severe ulcerative colitis
pmc-10757473.creator: Patrick Hilley, Danny Con, Matthew C Choy, Ashish Srinivasan, Peter De Cruz
pmc-10757473.description: Recent data, indicating that inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) may be a risk factor for future chronic kidney disease, highlight the need to study the safety and clinical effectiveness of advanced IBD therapies in patients with end stage renal disease (ESRD), defined as an eGFR <15 mL/min/1.73m2.

A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). stent otorrhea should raise suspicion of acquired cholesteatoma

Foul-smelling otorrhea and hearing loss are common presentations of cholesteatoma.2 This diagnosis should be considered with recurrent or persistent otorrhea for more than 2 weeks.

pmc-11640394.title: The Role of Gene Expression Profiling in the Management of Cutaneous Squamous Cell Cancer: A Review
pmc-11640394.creator: Ryan A. Durgham, Joel Badders, Shaun A. Nguyen, Lindsay Olinde, John Pang, Cherie-Ann O. Nathan
pmc-11640394.description: Simple SummaryCutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) is a common type of skin cancer. While most cases are curable, some can spread to other parts of the body, becoming life-threatening. Currently, physicians use physical features of the tumor to predict which cases might spread, but this method is not always accurate.

pmc-11679215.title: Iodine Deficiency Exacerbates Thyroidal and Neurological Effects of Developmental Perchlorate Exposure in the Neonatal and Adult Rat
pmc-11679215.creator: Mary E. Gilbert, MaryAnn G. Hawks, Kiersten S. Bell, Wendy Oshiro, Carmen Wood, Barbara Jane George, Ryne Thomas, Jermaine Ford
pmc-11679215.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Thyroid hormones (THs) require iodine for biosynthesis and play critical roles in brain development. Perchlorate is an environmental contaminant that reduces serum THs by blocking the uptake of iodine from the blood to the thyroid gland. Using a pregnant rodent model, we examined the impact of maternal exposure to perchlorate under conditions of dietary iodine deficiency (ID) on the brain and behavior of offspring.

pmc-12430604.title: Adherence to the Mediterranean Diet Among Primary School Children in the Tagus Lezíria Region, Portugal: A Study on Eating Habits
pmc-12430604.creator: Vanda Lopes de Andrade, Inês Ferrão, Maria Figueiredo, Igor Dias, Paula Pinto, Paula Ruivo
pmc-12430604.description: Background/Objectives: Poor dietary habits remain a significant public health concern, highlighting the need to promote healthy and sustainable eating patterns, especially in childhood and adolescence. This study assessed the eating habits of primary school children in the Tagus Lezíria region, focusing on adherence to the Mediterranean Diet (MD), recognized for its health and environmental benefits.

pmc-12684159.title: Impact of clinical decision support systems (CDSS) on clinical outcomes and healthcare delivery in low- and middle-income countries: protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12684159.creator: Garima Jain, Anand Bodade, Sanghamitra Pati
pmc-12684159.description: AbstractIntroductionClinical decision support systems (CDSS) are used to improve clinical and service outcomes, yet evidence from low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) is dispersed. This protocol outlines methods to quantify the impact of CDSS on patient and healthcare delivery outcomes in LMICs.

pmc-12729719.title: Comparative Assessment of Microbial Colonization and Tissue Reaction Among Three Suture Materials: A Randomized Controlled Trial
pmc-12729719.creator: José Manuel Alarcón Cordovilla, María Victoria Olmedo-Gaya, María Teresa Arias-Moliz, Adela Baca García, David Sánchez-Porras, María Pilar Quesada-García, María Nuria Romero-Olid, Sigrun Eick
pmc-12729719.description: Background: The aim of this study was to evaluate and compare the bacterial colonization, cytotoxicity, immune response, and clinical parameters of three different suture materials: multifilament silk (Silk®), monofilament nylon (Daclon®), and expanded polytetrafluoroethylene monofilament (PTFE®), in surgical extractions of impacted mandibular third molars.

pmc-13030689.title: A Fully Automated Deep Learning Pipeline for Anatomical Landmark Localization on Three-Dimensional Pelvic Surface Scans
pmc-13030689.creator: Woosu Choi, Jun-Su Jang
pmc-13030689.description: Accurate identification of anatomical landmarks on three-dimensional (3D) pelvic surface scans is essential for musculoskeletal assessment, yet manual procedures remain limited by operator dependence and soft tissue variability. This study presents a fully automated deep learning pipeline for localizing anatomical landmarks on the posterior pelvic region from raw 3D point cloud data.

pmc-13065261.title: Evaluating the Kidney Research Scientist Core Education and National Training (KRESCENT) Program: A 20-Year Qualitative Thematic Analysis
pmc-13065261.creator: Ian D. Petula, Alison F. Chung, Jamie E. Knight, Sunny Hartwig, Adeera Levin, Theone S. E. Paterson
pmc-13065261.description: Background:The Kidney Research Scientist Core Education and National Training (KRESCENT) program was established to enhance kidney research capacity in Canada by providing salary support and specialized training for kidney researchers in Canada. This study is a qualitative evaluation to gain insight into participants’ experiences in the program.

pmc-13319546.title: An event-related potentials account of brain predictive coding
pmc-13319546.creator: Carlos M Gómez, Antonio Arjona, Francisco J Ruíz-Martínez, Manuel Muñoz-Caracuel, Vanesa Muñoz, Elena I Rodriguez-Martinez
pmc-13319546.description: Predictive coding is a theory that tries to account for how the brain processes in an anticipatory manner the expected stimuli, and reorganizes the underlying neural networks as a consequence of the outcome of predictions: Correct or incorrect. EEG has the advantage of making a continuous and almost instantaneous record of brain activity.

pmc-13341363.title: Inflammatory Cytokines Impair Glucagon Expression and Secretion in Pancreatic α‐Cells
pmc-13341363.creator: Caroline Bickelmann, Cedric Wilden, Leticia Prates‐Roma, Matthias W Laschke, Emmanuel Ampofo, Selina Wrublewsky
pmc-13341363.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). AimsInsulin resistance and obesity‐associated inflammation are key drivers in the pathogenesis of Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Whilst inflammatory cytokines are well known to impair β‐cell function, their impact on pancreatic α‐cells and glucagon (GCG) regulation remains poorly understood.

pmc-13604604.title: Behavioral Dynamics of Zebrafish Under Hydrodynamic Stimuli Induced by Magnetic Microactuator in Microfluidics
pmc-13604604.creator: Dineshkumar Loganathan, Pu-Hsiang Wang, Chia-Yuan Chen
pmc-13604604.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Behavioral investigation in zebrafish is essential for understanding adaptive responses, where learning represents a key process influenced by external stimuli. The applied stimulus plays a critical role in shaping such responses, therefore making physiologically relevant stimulation strategies important. Hydrodynamic stimuli represent one such modality, providing a natural and non-invasive means of activating mechanosensory responses in aquatic organisms, thereby enabling behavioral manipulation in microfluidic environments.
